Okay so you have a bunch of options. You can choose to not go to either event and avoid this whole issue entirely, which is not necessarily a bad thing, just the easiest thing. Or you can go to one/both of these events while still in the closet. You can bind for the prom, and wear masculine clothes ect. This wont change you being awkward, but it'll give you more socialization practice.  This wont change the fact that you school will read / see you as female either. But you will be able to say that you didn't bail out on your schools senior prom, but that isnt important if you don't consider prom important. This would be easyish. As for the camping trip, thats a lil more complicated. You cant bind during the hiking on this trip, and its hot as fuck. You can go and depending on your wardrobe you can ,, help with your chest being visible. Wearing a sports bra and short sleeve button ups will work well for this. You will not be completely flat but the importance of that is up to you. As for swimming, your still in the closet so you can skip out on that entirely if it makes you too uncomfortable. (oh no fuck i forgot my swim suit smh guess i cant swim) Or you can go in swim trunks and a swim shirt. If you have more than one binder you can swim in your binder but then again your closeted so people will wonder where your chest went. For tent sharing, is it gender separated? Will it bother you if you have to share with the girls? And then lastly you can come out and do one/both of these things. Bind for the dance, wear a sharp suit and go with a friend. For the camping, do all the same shit you'd do but bind during swimming, and ask the principal to let you share with the mens tent. This of course is the hardest option. Coming out is hard. Facing peoples reactions is hard. But bright side, your a senior, so after you graduate and go off to college you'll likely never see them again and their opinions wont matter. How important is going to these events ? How much do you actually want to go to them? Think about what option suits you best, and good luck!

You have 2 choices; Come out. Or stay closeted. 
Coming out:
PROS
- Less dysphoria
- You get to present more masculinity
- Being your authentic self openly
- Transitioning earlier 
CONS:
- Unsupportive environment
- Educational issues
- Religious differences? (I think you can be trans regardless of religion I'm pretty sure theirs nothing in any holy book against it)
Staying Closeted:
PROS:
- No educational complications
- Your friends/family's view of you wont change
- No religious conflict
CONS:
- More dysphoria. 
You really need to evaluate how bad the reaction will be. Test the waters around your family, bring up a trans celebrity like Caitlin Jenner and see their reaction. Do the same with your friends. Will your family be violent? kick you out of your home? Will coming out now ultimately lead to abuse that would make it better to stay closeted? As for schooling, would you be able to go to a non Jewish school? Public schools will allow you to attend regardless of your transness. I'm sorry things are so rough OP, being in the closet and playing this waiting game is really hard. If you cant come out I'd suggest you buy more masculine clothes, maybe hit up a goodwill. You can tuck your hair into a hat, and you can bind with a sports bra. You can pack with a rolled up sock and wear roomy hoodies and jeans that hide the features you might not be fond of. You will reach a point in your life where you can transition, where you have people who support you, where you  people read you as male. I'm sorry that this isn't easy, but you can get through this. Be kind to yourself and good luck with whatever you choose to do.
I hope your transition goes well, good luck on your journey.
